item.title: Sometimes You Just Need the Right Props to Make Your Point: Data Center Reps Face the Guillotine, Flee Public Hearing
item.description: For towns and cities across the country looking for ways to tell data center developers that their projects aren’t welcome in their communities, the fine folks of Salem, Oregon seem to have found a very efficient way to get their message across: Pull up to public hearings with a guillotine. Last month, representatives from Verrus, a California-based data center development company, made the trek up to the city of 180,000 to pitch a planned $5.1 billion server farm that would move into 75 acres of state-owned property. According to the Salem Reporter, they were greeted by hundreds of citizens, most of whom showed up to tell Verrus to shove it. One person in particular got attention: a guy who put a guillotine on a trailer and rode it around outside of the Salem Public Library’s Loucks Auditorium where the meeting was taking place. It seems the message was received. Per the Salem Reporter, Verrus’ representatives left the hearing early because they “did not feel safe.” Some pro-data center voices did stay, including Aaron Stickney, the co-founder of SilverSphere Capital that is financing the project. When he spoke, members of the public reportedly jeered and called him a liar. When members of the public took the mic and expressed their concerns and vented their frustrations with what seems to be a clandestine and rushed project. In particular, they seemed to take issue with the fact that the city of Salem’s representatives signed a non-disclosure agreeement with Verrus when the project was first brought to them, which, according to the Oregonian, left the citizens in the dark for more than a year before they were informed about the effort—a common tactic that data center developers have taken to railroad communities and keep the public out of the conversation until it’s too late. Seems like another reason that Verrus used the NDA was to cover its own ass. Reportedly, representatives of the company were unable to answer any questions about water or electricity usage associated with the project, and the company has yet to submit its land use application to the city. While a lot of ire was directed at the developer, it was not exactly a banner showing for the city council. Per the Salem Reporter, one council member didn’t show up for the event and sent a fill-in to take their spot, and Mayor Julie Hoy made the decision to attend remotely rather than in-person. By the end of the event, the residents of Salem emerged with a few tentative wins on its ledger. The council vote unanimously to pass a motion to explore banning non-disclosure agreements with developers and another to form a data center task force for the city. According to the Salem Reporter, the council also set up a second hearing that took place earlier this week and led to a temporary moratorium that will prevent any data center projects from moving forward for at least 120 days. Turns out the public has more power than you’d imagine, especially when they show up with the blade ready to drop. https://gizmodo.com/data-center-reps-face-the-guillotine-flee-public-hearing-2000795939

item.title: How to tell your kings from your queens
item.description:
This is a very small fun fact I wanted to share about monarch butterflies. This is a little Facebook post I made yesterday. Butterflies are my favorite animal, so I always feel really happy when I get to be near one. I’m especially overjoyed when I can convince them to rest on my finger for a little while. In my post, I mentioned that I could tell this was a male monarch due to his wing size and pattern. In my personal experience, butterflies are often immediately assumed to be females, so I decided to clarify that I could tell he was a male. You might be wondering how to tell the difference between a male and female monarch butterfly? Like the meme says, male wings are slightly larger, have two unique little blotches, and have thinner veins in their wing pattern.
Here’s a closeup of my temporary little buddy before he flew away for better nectar lol.
I did a super close up of the butterfly I saw yesterday morning, complete with excessive red (or blue in this case) circles and arrows. According to the Monarch Watch website, these two extra blotches are actually made of special scales that release pheromones when looking for a mate. It’s the butterfly version of cologne.
Image Source: Monarch Watch Website (see sources cited . I wonder why the veins in the wings are thinner. I didn’t see an explanation for that, but it’s entirely possible that I just missed it.
Image Source: Monarch Joint Venture (see sources cited) . Looking at this, I think I might have the wing size backwards. I’ve read that the male monarch wings are larger, but the comparison images I keep finding suggest the opposite. I also haven’t been at 100% as of late, so I could very well be looking at this wrong.
If you ever want to know the sex of the monarch butterfly in your gardens, just look for this little extra blotch, and the veins in their wings! I hope you enjoyed this very tiny fun fact. It made me very happy! . . SOURCES CITED: Monarch Watch Website: https://www.monarchwatch.org/biology/ Monarch Joint Venture Website: https://monarchjointventure.org/monarch-biology/vital-statistics-and-measuring

item.title: Evidence of a federal crime? We will know soon!
item.description: Senator John Boozman claims he spoke with Mitch McConnell on the night of August 5 and received authorization to cast McConnell’s proxy votes the following day. That makes one question extremely important: Was Mitch McConnell actually capable of speaking with Boozman and authorizing those votes on August 5? If McConnell was unable to communicate and did not authorize those votes, then Boozman’s statement would be false and votes were attempted in a U.S. Senate committee in another senator’s name without his authorization. Could that constitute a federal crime? If so, it needs to be investigated. There should be a written record. Release McConnell’s proxy authorization and put this question to rest. The American people deserve proof that the votes being cast in the United States Senate are actually authorized by the senators they are attributed to.

item.title: Southwest Blocks ICE Agent From Arresting Passenger ... United Paged Passenger To The Gate—Then ICE Agents Surrounded Her.
item.description: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent trying to board a Southwest Airlines flight in Dallas was reportedly stopped by a gate agent who demanded a judicial warrant before allowing the agent onto the aircraft. The July 25 incident could signal a growing pushback from airlines as immigration enforcement at U.S. airports increases. ICE has been arresting more travelers at airports amid a new information-sharing arrangement with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), which has been providing ICE with passenger flight information. Now, a report from The Wall Street Journal suggests Southwest employees are drawing a line when ICE agents attempt to access aircraft or passenger information without the documentation the airline requires. Southwest Airlines Pushes Back Against ICE Enforcement At Dallas Love Field Airport The incident happened at Dallas Love Field Airport on July 25 when an ICE agent attempted to board a Southwest flight headed from Dallas to Orlando to make an arrest, but a Southwest gate agent reportedly refused to allow the agent onto the aircraft without a judicial warrant signed by a judge. Southwest employees also reportedly refused to provide ICE with passenger information or allow agents to view a computer screen displaying passenger information as travelers boarded the flight. The ICE agent reportedly had an administrative warrant, which was signed by an ICE supervisor rather than an independent judge. https://www.thetravel.com/southwest-airlines-is-the-first-to-stand-up-to-ice-employee-blocks-agent-from-arresting-passenger/ United Paged Passenger To The Gate—Then ICE Agents Surrounded Her. Now She’s Suing The Airline A United Airlines passenger says the carrier repeatedly paged her to the gate for a boarding pass problem, but there was nothing wrong with her boarding pass. It was all to lure her out in the open so that three plainclothes ICE agents could take her into custody. She spent the next 11 days in immigration detention. Now she and her husband are suing United, arguing that it used the authority passengers place in an airline announcement to lure her into an ambush. The is legal case does.. not appear strong, even if her legal presence was a lot firmer than you’d expect from the ICE operation and subsequent detention. https://viewfromthewing.com/united-paged-passenger-to-the-gate-then-ice-agents-surrounded-her-now-shes-suing-the-airline/
